# landscape_LA_direct

**AIDA-Scout S1b (landscape scalar cascades), benchmark `L-A`** -- generated by
`landscape/make_processes.py`.

A single hidden scalar, produced directly by gluon fusion through its Higgs admixture, cascades within the hidden sector until it reaches scalars below the pair-production threshold, which then decay to the Standard Model. The whole event is one such chain: **about 6 partons at a median 4 GeV**, sharing whatever mass the produced scalar had (mean 4.7 GeV).

**This point has nothing to trigger on at all.** With the B-meson term still on, only **3.2% of events contained a single 30 GeV jet**, and the median HT over such jets was 0; without it the partons are softer still. It is not that it fails the menu -- there is no hadronic object in the event to fail with.

Reference: R. T. D'Agnolo, M. Ettengruber, L.-T. Wang, *Landscapes at
Colliders*, arXiv:2512.18001. The model is a Python port of the authors' Julia
code; see [`landscape/README.md`](../../landscape/README.md) for the port, its
eight-tier verification, and the deliberate deviations.

## Parameters

| | |
|---|---|
| N (number of singlet scalars) | 200 |
| lambda | 0.0001 |
| lambda' | 0.0001 |
| lambda'/lambda | 1 |
| M* | 10000 GeV |
| v2 | 221.4 GeV |
| mixing angle theta | 0.001 |
| mass spectrum | uniform on [0.7071, 10] GeV |
| **spectrum seed** | **424242** (one landscape realisation, fixed across jobs) |
| production | direct ggF (the Julia's B-meson term off, see below) |

## Normalisation

| | |
|---|---|
| cross section x BR | **2.924 pb** |
| BR(h -> BSM), physical (Gamma_SM = 4.1e-3 GeV) | 0.0001514 |
| BR(h -> BSM), Julia normalisation (Gamma_bb(pole) x 1.89) | 7.633e-05 |
| Higgs signal-strength bound | 0.1 -- **within** |

**The original code's B-meson production term is switched off here**
(`--no-bmeson-term` in the args file). The Julia's production sum adds
`1e-3 * bmesondecay` -- a dimensionless branching-ratio-like quantity -- to two
terms that are cross sections in barns (`ScalarProductionshare.jl` lines 66-81
and 143-153). Left in, it would contribute 1.124e+04 pb against 2.921 pb
of genuine direct production, a factor 3850, and because it is nonzero
only below 4.7 GeV it would also skew *which* scalar is produced. The authors'
L-A as written includes it; remove `--no-bmeson-term` from the args file to
reproduce that (1.125e+04 pb).


## Lifetimes

```
Lifetimes: L-A
  200 scalars, hidden-pair threshold 2*m_min = 1.549 GeV
  ctau over the whole spectrum: min 1.708e-11  median 4.865e-11  max 4.233e+00 mm
  above threshold (182 scalars, hidden pair channel open): median 4.203e-11 mm  max 1.488e-07 mm
  below threshold (18 scalars = 9.0%, mixing only): median 2.725e+00 mm  max 4.233e+00 mm  <-- DISPLACED
```

Every cascade *terminates* on a sub-threshold scalar, so this displacement is
not a tail -- it is where essentially all the visible partons come from.


## Why it evades (or does not evade) the Phase-2 L1 menu

| Seed | Threshold | Fires? |
|---|---|---|
| PuppiHT | 450 (constituents pT > 30) | no -- 0.10% |
| SinglePuppiJet | 230 | no -- 0.15% |
| QuadJet | 400,70,55,40,40 | no -- the 400 GeV HT leg already fails |
| DoubleTkMuon (BPH) | 2,2, abs(eta)<1.5, dR<1.4, OS, dz<1cm | no -- 0.0% |
| DoubleTkMuon (central) | 4,4 | no -- 0.0% |
| DoubleTkElectron | 25,12 | no -- no electrons in the cascade |
| DoubleTkIsoPhoton | 22,12 | no -- the photon channel is below 0.1% |
| DoublePuppiTau | 52,52 | no |
| PuppiETmiss | 200 | no -- nothing escapes but tau neutrinos |


## What is in the LHE

The hidden scalars are written into the record, not just the final partons.
They share one PDG id (9000006) and each carries its own mass and its own
`VTIMUP`, because an LHE has nowhere else to put a per-particle displacement
and the cascade's decay vertices are the physics.

`LesHouches:setLifetime = 1` in the card is load-bearing: it is Pythia's
default, but `= 2` silently discards `VTIMUP` and collapses every hidden-scalar
decay vertex to the origin, making the sample prompt with no error. Verified by
A/B: with `= 1` the scalar decay vertices reach 232 mm; with `= 2` they are all
exactly zero.

Colour is connected **locally**: each phi -> q qbar is its own singlet with one
fresh tag, each phi -> g g its own closed loop with two. Connecting colour
across the cascade would string the whole event together and materially change
the hadronic activity.

## Measured, truth level, 2000 events, no pileup

**Measured with the Julia's B-meson term still on.** It favoured scalars below
4.7 GeV; without it the partons are more numerous, softer and more displaced
(parton level, 2000 events: multiplicity 5.67 / 6, energy median 4.2 GeV,
85% with r_xy > 0.1 mm against 73%). Re-measure the showered rows.

| | |
|---|---|
| parton multiplicity, mean / median | 4.01 / 4 |
| parton energy, median | 8.1 GeV |
| charged multiplicity after showering, median | 33 |
| of which from the hard process | 2 |
| jets above 30 GeV, median | 0 |
| HT, median | 0 GeV |
| leading jet pT, median | 0 GeV |
| signal charged particles displaced > 0.1 mm | 96.4% |
| signal charged r_xy, median / 90% | 2.9 / 31 mm |

## Downstream limits

* `cards/delphes_card.dat` has **no d0 dependence** in its L1T tracking
  efficiencies -- they are functions of pt and eta only. The sample is correct
  at truth level, but the chain will not reproduce the loss of displaced tracks
  at L1. This matters most for `landscape_LB_higgs_displaced` and
  `landscape_LA_direct`.
* Delphes drops particles produced outside the tracker (R = 1.29 m, half-length
  3 m).
* **L1 menu decision bits are not produced here.** No CMSSW Phase-2 emulator
  exists in this repository; the menu column above is truth-level Pythia against
  the offline thresholds, which is an upper bound on what the real menu sees.

## Running

```bash
apptainer exec --bind $simdir \
  /cvmfs/unpacked.cern.ch/registry.hub.docker.com/jmduarte/mapyde:latest \
  sh $simdir/run.sh landscape_LA_direct <nevents> <seed> $simdir False
```

This point uses the **pythia** branch of `run.sh`, with the landscape LHE
pre-step in front of it. `run.sh` runs `landscape.make_lhe` with the arguments
in `landscape_LA_direct_lhe_args.dat`, writes the parton-level summary to
`outdir/parton_level.txt`, and then hands the LHE to the same Pythia -> HepMC
-> PU 200 -> Delphes -> parquet chain every other point uses.

To produce the LHE on its own, outside the job:

```bash
python3 -m landscape.make_lhe --benchmark L-A --fast-branching --no-bmeson-term \
    --nevents 10000 --seed 1234 --out L-A.lhe --fragment L-A.cmnd
```
